facts.statement: The genus Acresuchus was described by Souza-Filho and colleagues in 2018.
Acresuchus lived during the Late Miocene epoch.
Acresuchus, meaning "Acre crocodile", is an extinct genus of medium-sized caiman found in western Brazil and Venezuela.
facts.quote: Acresuchus ("Acre crocodile") is an extinct monospecific genus of medium-sized caiman from the Late Miocene of western Brazil and Venezuela.

facts.statement: The genus Acresuchus contains only one known species, Acresuchus pachytemporalis.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Acresuchus pachytemporalis.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen UFAC-2507 is a nearly complete skull found in the Solimões Formation in Acre.
facts.quote: The hypodigm of Acresuchus consists of the holotype, UFAC-2507, a nearly complete skull, and several referred specimens, most found in Niteroi, located in the Solimões Formation in Acre.

facts.statement: A skull fragment specimen was found in the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela.
facts.quote: Another specimen, MCNUSB-PB-02FU-RS43, a skull fragment, was found in the middle member of the Urumaco Formation in Venezuela.

facts.statement: Acresuchus possesses large supratemporal fenestrae, which may be adaptations for large body size.
facts.quote: Acresuchus shares traits with Purussaurus that may have been adaptations to large body size, such as large supratemporal fenestrae.

facts.statement: Large supratemporal fenestrae in Acresuchus may have aided in quicker prey capture and thermoregulation.
facts.quote: These provided quicker capture of prey and better thermoregulation.

facts.statement: Acresuchus likely had a diet similar to the living black caiman due to shared features and size.
facts.quote: Acresuchus shares many features with the living black caiman, including size, which suggests it would have a similar diet.

facts.statement: Juvenile Acresuchus likely preyed on small invertebrates, while adults ate fish and small to medium-sized mammals.
facts.quote: If this assumption is correct, juvenile Acresuchus would have preyed on small invertebrates, with adults feeding on fish and small to medium-sized mammals.

facts.statement: Blunt teeth at the back of the skull suggest Acresuchus may have eaten hard-shelled animals.
facts.quote: The teeth at the back of the skull in Acresuchus are blunt, indicating that it may have also eaten hard-shelled animals.

facts.statement: Acresuchus is classified as a member of the subfamily Caimaninae, closely related to Purussaurus.
facts.quote: The analysis found it to be a member of Caimaninae closely related to Purussaurus, which was confirmed by subsequent studies.

facts.statement: The parent group of Acresuchus is the genus Jacarea.
Acresuchus belongs to the family Alligatoridae.
Acresuchus lived from the Tortonian to the Messinian stages, between 11.63 and 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Tortonian to Messinian (11.63 to 5.333 million years ago)
